key_insight: A high-order FR/CPR solver coupled with an actuator-line model can predict rotating-blade aerodynamics on fixed Cartesian grids without resolving blade geometry, while retaining good accuracy for VAWT wakes and power output.
engineering_relevance: This provides a geometry-free, computationally efficient route for simulating wind-turbine performance and wakes, making coarse-grid design studies and large-scale wind-energy analyses more practical.
method: FR/CPR flow solver on a fixed Cartesian grid
Rotating actuator-line model with isotropic Gaussian force projection
Modified Boeing-Vertol dynamic stall model plus DMST inflow correction
evidence_signal: The framework was validated against experimental near-wake data and LES-ALM results, with mean wake profiles in good agreement and power-coefficient predictions within about 6% of high-fidelity 3D LES-ALM near optimal operating conditions.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on choosing a sufficiently resolved Gaussian kernel and applying the coarse-mesh/DMST corrections correctly; otherwise induction feedback and force projection errors can distort the inflow and wake.
paper_title: A High-Order Flux Reconstruction Actuator-Line Framework for Rotating-Blade Aerodynamics on Fixed Cartesian Grids
